Dialog

A modal window for one short task that must be finished or cancelled before the reader goes on.

Status: draft

Examples

When to use it

  • For a short task the reader starts from the current view and finishes in one step, such as renaming a branch.
  • To ask a question the view cannot go on without, with one primary action and Cancel.

When not to use it

  • To confirm deleting or discarding something. Use the confirm dialog.
  • For a longer form, filters or the details of an item. Use a sheet.
  • For supplementary content beside a control that should not block the page. Use a popover.
  • To report that something happened. Use a toast, or an alert for a result that stays.

Variants

default
No modifier class. The dialog grows with its content and scrolls as a whole once it reaches the height of the screen.
scroll ds-dialog--scroll
A body that may be long, such as a list of files. The title and the footer stay in place and the body scrolls between two rules.

Accessibility

  • Use a dialog element with aria-labelledby pointing at ds-dialog__title, an h2. When the body is one short text, point aria-describedby at it.
  • Open it with the one line document.getElementById("dialog-id").showModal(). That call traps focus, makes the page behind inert, closes on Escape and returns focus to the opener when the dialog closes. Do not write the open attribute yourself, which shows the dialog without any of that: the open examples carry it only so they are drawn in the gallery. The closed example is the markup an app ships: the dialog without the open attribute, and its opener.
  • The opener is a button with command="show-modal" and commandfor="dialog-id", as in the closed example. Where the browser supports invoker commands it opens the dialog with no script.
  • The showModal() fallback goes in the app's own script file, never in an onclick attribute or an inline script: one click listener on the opener that calls showModal() on the dialog its commandfor names, added only when "command" in HTMLButtonElement.prototype is false, so a browser with invoker commands does not open the dialog twice. A framework app calls showModal() from the button's click handler through a ref and leaves the two attributes out.
  • Wrap the content in a form with method="dialog" and the class ds-dialog__panel. Each footer button is a submit button with a value. Pressing one closes the dialog with no script, and the app reads dialog.returnValue in a close event listener. To validate or save before closing, handle the form's submit event and call preventDefault().
  • The primary button comes first in the footer and Cancel second, so Enter in a field takes the primary action. Cancel carries formnovalidate so it closes a form with an empty required field.
  • showModal() moves focus to the first focusable element, or to the one that has the autofocus attribute. Tab stays inside the dialog.
  • A dialog has one primary button. It is a view of its own, so the page behind may have its own.
  • With ds-dialog--scroll, if the body holds no control, give ds-dialog__body tabindex="0", role="group" and an aria-label so the keyboard can scroll it.
  • While saving, set aria-busy="true" on the primary button, change its label to say what is happening and disable Cancel. If it fails, keep the dialog open and say what happened and what to do, in the field's error or in an alert inside the body.
